chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim from Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim from whoever narrated to him from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The sick person prays standing; if he cannot do that, he prays sitting; if he cannot do that, he prays lying on his back. He says Takbir then recites. When he intends to bow (Ruku'), he closes his eyes, then glorifies (Allah); when he has glorified, he opens his eyes, and the opening of his eyes is the raising of his head from Ruku'. When he intends to prostrate (Sujud), he closes his eyes, then glorifies; when he has glorified, he opens his eyes, and the opening of his eyes is the raising of his head from Sujud. Then he recites the Tashahhud and turns for Salam.
ai.seo_question: How does a sick person perform Ruku and Sujud if they cannot move their head physically?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific prayer protocol for a patient lying on their back (*mustalqi*), where eye movements substitute for physical bowing and prostration, a method widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence for those unable to move their limbs. It highlights the principle of *takbir* (glorification) accompanying these gestures, ensuring the validity of prayer even in extreme weakness, while concluding with the standard *tashahhud* and *salam*.
